title: ECFR’s summer entertainment list 2026 – European Council on Foreign Relations
gist: ECFR's 2026 summer reading list is a soft-signal read on what Europe's foreign-policy staff are preoccupied with: the internal social fabric of the United States, anti-government radicalisation as a precursor to Trumpism, Ukraine on the eve of invasion, the opioid crisis, and Havel's 'living in truth' as a template for a 'world of unorder'. Investor content is minimal; the value is in elite-attention signals rather than analysis.

insights.claim: Mark Carney's speech at Davos revived attention to Václav Havel's 1978 essay 'The Power of the Powerless', which ECFR staff read as a prescription for today's 'world of unorder': reject conformity, stand for truth, and build parallel communities around a bare-minimum shared values floor.
insights.speaker: Mireia Faro Sarrats
insights.so_what: Watch for dissident/values-based framing entering Western political and corporate rhetoric — it usually precedes harder-edged policy on authoritarian counterparties.
insights.quote: This is exactly what Havel brings to today’s world of unorder: reject conformity and the ruthlessness dictated by others, stand for truth
insights.locator: “The Power of the Powerless”, an essay by Václav Havel

insights.claim: An ECFR policy fellow argues the 2014 armed standoff between the libertarian Mormon Bundy ranching family and the US federal government outside Las Vegas was a direct precursor to the Trumpian years, and that it shows how deep American distrust of government runs.
insights.speaker: Mireia Faro Sarrats
insights.so_what: European institutional analysts now treat US anti-state radicalisation as structural, not episodic — a bearish input for assumptions of US policy continuity.
insights.quote: it reveals just how deep American distrust of the government runs, and how far people will go in the name of “freedom”

insights.claim: ECFR held its Annual Council Meeting 2026 in Vienna, and the institution frames the year's first half as 'dominated by uncertainty, crises and conflict'.
insights.speaker: Mireia Faro Sarrats
insights.so_what: Baseline read on the mood of Europe's leading foreign-policy network heading into H2 2026.
insights.locator: Summer is here, and with it ECFR’s entertainment list

insights.claim: ECFR contributors' 2026 picks skew heavily toward the United States' domestic social conditions — slavery and racial trauma, Gulf Coast poverty, opioid capture of regulators, rural anti-federal militancy — rather than toward Washington policy.
insights.speaker: Mireia Faro Sarrats
insights.so_what: European policy elites are increasingly modelling US political risk from the bottom up, which tends to produce lower confidence in US commitments.
insights.quote: This year, our contributors’ choices take us to the US—but far beyond the newspaper headlines—to learn about the country’s people, their fights and their struggles.
insights.locator: This year, our contributors’ choices take us to the US

insights.claim: Gloria Steinem's reporting method is offered as an analytical model: focusing on country capitals overshadows the lives of ordinary people and paints a distorted picture of a country, with the true character of a place found on its streets and roads.
insights.speaker: Mireia Faro Sarrats
insights.so_what: A usable due-diligence heuristic: capital-city sourcing systematically biases country risk assessments.
insights.quote: focus on country capitals often overshadow the lives of ordinary people and paint a distorted picture of a country
insights.locator: “My Life on the Road” is a great book for anyone

insights.claim: The Sackler family's OxyContin business is framed as a story of greed and impunity in which philanthropy coexisted with responsibility for the US opioid crisis, and investigative journalism was the corrective mechanism.
insights.speaker: Mireia Faro Sarrats
insights.so_what: Reputational-capture narratives around pharma remain live in European policy circles — relevant to litigation and ESG screening risk.
insights.locator: “Empire of Pain: The Secret History of the Sackler Dynasty”

insights.claim: 'Salvage the Bones' is recommended for the argument that disasters are never equal: Hurricane Katrina is only one of several forces threatening a poor Mississippi family already abandoned by protective systems.
insights.speaker: Mireia Faro Sarrats
insights.so_what: Distributional framing of climate disaster losses — the political logic behind adaptation-funding and insurance-of-last-resort debates.
insights.quote: It is a powerful reminder that disasters are never equal, and that for some, the storm began long before Katrina made landfall.

insights.claim: Christopher Nolan's big-screen version of the Odyssey reached cinemas in mid-July 2026, prompting renewed interest in Emily Wilson's translation and in Ralph Fiennes's 2024 film 'The Return'.
insights.speaker: Mireia Faro Sarrats
insights.so_what: Concrete release timing for a major 2026 tentpole plus the classics-publishing halo effect it drives.

insights.claim: Maria Reva's 'Endling' centres on Ukraine's booming marriage industry and a road trip across the country on the brink of Russia's full-scale invasion, treating gender, survival and resilience as the war's underlying themes.
insights.speaker: Mireia Faro Sarrats
insights.so_what: Signal that ECFR staff frame Ukraine through societal endurance rather than battlefield lines — consistent with long-war expectations.
